body:
## Summary

`MoeWNA16Method`'s weight loader splits the fused `w13_qzeros` (gate/up) zero-points at `shard_size // 2`, which is only correct for 4-bit. `w13_qzeros` is packed along the intermediate dim by `bit8_pack_factor` (`8 // weight_bits`), so the w1/w3 boundary is in **packed** units — `shard_size // bit8_pack_factor`. For **8-bit asymmetric GPTQ MoE** (`bit8_pack_factor == 1`, `has_zp=True`) the param's intermediate dim is `2 * intermediate` (unpacked), but each shard's loaded tensor is `intermediate` wide, so writing into a half-width `[: shard_size // 2]` slice raises a shape mismatch at load. The common 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ path is unaffected (`bit8_pack_factor == 2`, so `shard_size // 2 == shard_size // bit8_pack_factor`).

## Fix
My fix is as follows:
`moe_wna16.py` — split `w13_qzeros` at `shard_size // layer.quant_config.bit8_pack_factor` instead of the hardcoded `shard_size // 2`. Only `w13_qzeros` is affected: qweight/scales aren't packed on that axis, and `w2_qzeros` isn't shard-split.

## Impact for various backends

Platform-independent: the defect is in load-time weight-loader code with no CUDA/ROCm gate, and WNA16 INT4/INT8 GPTQ/AWQ MoE runs on ROCm (Triton fused-MoE). So this **affects AMD** as well as CUDA. Failure mode is a **loud load-time error** (shape mismatch), not silent wrong output, in the narrow 8-bit-asymmetric config. (Marlin doesn't support asymmetric GPTQ, so `sym=False` MoE routes to `moe_wna16` by construction — this path can't be diverted to Marlin.)

## Test plan

Added `test_moe_wna16_w13_qzeros_shard_split_int8_asym_gptq` in `tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py` — CPU-only. Builds a real 8-bit GPTQ `MoeWNA16Method`, runs `create_weights`, drives the actual weight loader for the w1/w3 shards, and asserts both load without error and land in the correct halves.

```
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py -q
# 16 passed, 9 skipped (CUDA/humming-gated)
# new test PASSES on the fix; FAILS when reverted to `shard_size // 2` (guards the exact regression)

ruff check <both files>          # All checks passed
ruff format --check <both files> # already formatted
```

## Model evaluation

No full-model eval — this fixes a checkpoint-**load** failure (weight placement / shape), not inference math, and the 4-bit path is provably unchanged (`shard_size // 2 == shard_size // bit8_pack_factor` when `bit8_pack_factor == 2`), so no accuracy regression is possible.

I did attempt to do an end-to-end run by quantizing a small MoE (OLMoE-1B-7B) to 8-bit asymmetric GPTQ, but it is blocked in this vLLM environment: **transformers 5.x fuses MoE experts into a single module**, while the GPTQ tooling (`gptqmodel`) quantizes per-expert submodules that no longer exist — so no MoE can be freshly GPTQ-quantized here without downgrading transformers. No public 8-bit *asymmetric* GPTQ MoE checkpoint exists to load directly either.

Evidence in lieu of an eval: the added unit test drives the **real** `create_weights` + `moe_wna16_weight_loader` on the actual code path (fails before the fix with the exact shape mismatch, passes after), and verifies the loaded zero-points land in the correct gate/up halves. A reviewer with an 8-bit-asym GPTQ MoE checkpoint (or a transformers-4.x quantization env) can confirm end-to-end load.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open/merged PRs touching this area:
- #51645 (open) — fixes `create_weights` **allocation** along the group dimension for non-divisible group sizes; different axis, doesn't touch the loader split.
- #51125 (merged) — sized `w13` allocation by `w13_num_shards`; established that pattern but left this loader split hardcoded.

Neither of these two PRs addresses the packed-unit shard boundary fixed here.
title: [Bugfix] Fix moe_wna16 w13 zero-point shard split for 8-bit asym GPTQ MoE
